question_text: Which of the following correctly describes dose response?

options.D: Uncertainty factors (UFs) are applied to NOAEL or BMD to derive RfDs or RfCs

explanation: Uncertainty factors (UFs) are applied to NOAEL or BMD to derive RfDs or RfCs. Standard UFs: 10x interspecies, 10x intraspecies, 3-10x LOAEL-to-NOAEL

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes species selection?

options.A: The rat is the most commonly used species in acute toxicity studies
options.C: Only one species needed for all studies
options.D: Species selection based solely on cost

explanation: The rat is the most commonly used species in acute toxicity studies. Mice, rabbits, and guinea pigs also used per regulatory requirements

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes species selection?

options.A: Non-rodent species (dogs, NHPs) are required in subchronic studies for drugs intended for chronic use
options.B: Species selection based solely on cost
options.C: Only one species needed for all studies

explanation: Non-rodent species (dogs, NHPs) are required in subchronic studies for drugs intended for chronic use. Provides assessment in a second species

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes statistical?

options.A: Cochran-Armitage trend test assesses dose-related trends in tumor incidence
options.D: Pairwise always more powerful than trend

explanation: Cochran-Armitage trend test assesses dose-related trends in tumor incidence. More powerful than pairwise comparisons when dose-response exists

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes statistical?

options.A: Historical control data account for spontaneous tumor rates varying by strain, sex, and facility
options.C: Pairwise always more powerful than trend

explanation: Historical control data account for spontaneous tumor rates varying by strain, sex, and facility. Essential for interpreting tumor findings in bioassays

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes quality assurance?

options.A: Raw data can be destroyed after study
options.C: QA unit must be independent of the study director with access to all study records
options.D: Study director also serves as QA

explanation: QA unit must be independent of the study director with access to all study records. Inspects studies at intervals and reports to management

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes quality assurance?

options.B: Study director also serves as QA
options.C: Raw data must be archived for minimum 10 years for FDA-regulated studies

explanation: Raw data must be archived for minimum 10 years for FDA-regulated studies. Includes all original observations, records, and photographs

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes quality assurance?

options.B: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are required for all GLP-compliant studies
options.D: Study director also serves as QA

explanation: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are required for all GLP-compliant studies. SOPs ensure consistency and reproducibility of methods

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes membrane transport?

options.B: Small hydrophilic molecules (up to about 600 Da) permeate membranes through aqueous pores via paracellular diffusion

explanation: Small hydrophilic molecules (up to about 600 Da) permeate membranes through aqueous pores via paracellular diffusion. Fick's law governs simple diffusion - chemicals move from higher to lower concentration without energy expenditure

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes membrane transport?

options.B: Lipid solubility is determined by the octanol/water partition coefficient (log P), with positive values indicating high lipid solubility

explanation: Lipid solubility is determined by the octanol/water partition coefficient (log P), with positive values indicating high lipid solubility. DDT has log P of 6.76, TCDD has log P of 7.05

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes membrane transport?

options.C: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation describes pH as a function of pKa for weak organic acids and bases

explanation: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation describes pH as a function of pKa for weak organic acids and bases. For acids: pH - pKa = log([ionized]/[nonionized]); for bases: pKa - pH = log([nonionized]/[ionized])

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes membrane transport?

options.A: Active transport requires energy, exhibits saturability, selectivity, and competitive inhibition

explanation: Active transport requires energy, exhibits saturability, selectivity, and competitive inhibition. Metabolic poisons block active transport by inhibiting ATP production

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes membrane transport?

options.C: Facilitated transport does not require energy input and is not affected by metabolic poisons

explanation: Facilitated transport does not require energy input and is not affected by metabolic poisons. Glucose transport from GI tract occurs via facilitated diffusion

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes transporters?

options.B: P-glycoprotein (MDR1/ABCB1) was the first active xenobiotic transporter identified, functioning as an efflux pump

explanation: P-glycoprotein (MDR1/ABCB1) was the first active xenobiotic transporter identified, functioning as an efflux pump. ABC transporter superfamily has 7 subfamilies with 49 genes in humans

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes transporters?

options.A: MRP2 and MRP3 efflux xenobiotic metabolites conjugated with glucuronic acid or glutathione

explanation: MRP2 and MRP3 efflux xenobiotic metabolites conjugated with glucuronic acid or glutathione. Acetaminophen glucuronide is a substrate for both MRP2 and MRP3

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes transporters?

options.A: BCRP (ABCG2) functions as homodimers linked by disulfide bridges at cysteine 603, with MW ~70 kDa

explanation: BCRP (ABCG2) functions as homodimers linked by disulfide bridges at cysteine 603, with MW ~70 kDa. MDR1 is ~170 kDa, MRP1 is ~190 kDa

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes transporters?

options.A: OATP1B1 polymorphisms decrease hepatic extraction, increasing systemic exposure to substrates like statins

explanation: OATP1B1 polymorphisms decrease hepatic extraction, increasing systemic exposure to substrates like statins. Decreased OATP1B1 function increases myopathy risk

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes transporters?

options.C: OCT2 mediates cisplatin uptake into kidney, contributing to dose-limiting nephrotoxicity

explanation: OCT2 mediates cisplatin uptake into kidney, contributing to dose-limiting nephrotoxicity. OCT1 mediates metformin uptake into liver

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.C: The three main barriers for toxicant absorption are the GI tract, lungs, and skin

explanation: The three main barriers for toxicant absorption are the GI tract, lungs, and skin. Only caustic/corrosive chemicals act directly at point of contact

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.B: Weak organic acids are absorbed more readily from the stomach (pH ~2) where they are nonionized

explanation: Weak organic acids are absorbed more readily from the stomach (pH ~2) where they are nonionized. Organic bases are absorbed predominantly in the intestine

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.A: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics
options.C: First-pass effect (presystemic elimination) removes chemicals before systemic circulation entry

explanation: First-pass effect (presystemic elimination) removes chemicals before systemic circulation entry. High first-pass effect limits toxic potential

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.B: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics
options.C: The small intestine increases surface area approximately 600-fold through villi and microvilli

explanation: The small intestine increases surface area approximately 600-fold through villi and microvilli. This overcomes low nonionized fraction at intestinal pH

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.A: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics
options.D: Oral absorption of heavy metals: ~10% lead, 4% manganese, 1.5% cadmium, 1% chromium

explanation: Oral absorption of heavy metals: ~10% lead, 4% manganese, 1.5% cadmium, 1% chromium. EDTA increases absorption of complexed metal ions

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.A: Particle absorption is inversely related to particle diameter; nanoparticles (<100 nm) are most readily absorbed
options.C: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics

explanation: Particle absorption is inversely related to particle diameter; nanoparticles (<100 nm) are most readily absorbed. Hydrophobic nonionized particles are more extensively absorbed

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.A: Intestinal microflora reduce nitroaromatic compounds to potentially carcinogenic aromatic amines

explanation: Intestinal microflora reduce nitroaromatic compounds to potentially carcinogenic aromatic amines. 2,6-dinitrotoluene is reduced to mutagenic 2,6-diaminotoluene

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.C: Pulmonary absorption of gases depends on blood:gas partition coefficient

explanation: Pulmonary absorption of gases depends on blood:gas partition coefficient. High coefficient (ethanol) = high absorption; low (N2O) = rapid equilibrium

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes absorption?

options.A: Grapefruit juice inhibits MDR1 through naringin, increasing bioavailability of co-administered drugs
options.C: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics

explanation: Grapefruit juice inhibits MDR1 through naringin, increasing bioavailability of co-administered drugs. Naringin is a flavonoid found in grapefruit

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes distribution?

options.C: Volume of distribution relates amount of chemical in body to concentration in blood/plasma

explanation: Volume of distribution relates amount of chemical in body to concentration in blood/plasma. Large Vd = extensive tissue distribution; small Vd = confinement to plasma

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding distribution EXCEPT:

options.D: DDT achieves high concentrations in fat but is not toxic to adipose tissue

explanation: DDT achieves high concentrations in fat but is not toxic to adipose tissue. Tissue of highest concentration is not necessarily the target organ

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding distribution EXCEPT:

options.D: Plasma proteins (especially albumin) serve as storage depot for acidic drugs and toxicants

explanation: Plasma proteins (especially albumin) serve as storage depot for acidic drugs and toxicants. Only unbound chemical is available for distribution and effects

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding distribution EXCEPT:

options.D: The blood-brain barrier limits entry of polar and large molecules into the CNS

explanation: The blood-brain barrier limits entry of polar and large molecules into the CNS. Tight junctions and P-gp efflux maintain the barrier

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding distribution EXCEPT:

options.C: Lipophilic chemicals can cross the placenta; P-gp provides protection by efflux back to maternal circulation

explanation: Lipophilic chemicals can cross the placenta; P-gp provides protection by efflux back to maternal circulation. Fetus is particularly vulnerable due to immature detoxification

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding excretion EXCEPT:

options.D: Urinary excretion involves glomerular filtration, active tubular secretion, and passive tubular reabsorption

explanation: Urinary excretion involves glomerular filtration, active tubular secretion, and passive tubular reabsorption. Molecules <60 kDa pass through glomerular pores; ionized forms are reabsorbed less

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding excretion EXCEPT:

options.B: Enterohepatic circulation involves biliary excretion followed by reabsorption from intestine

explanation: Enterohepatic circulation involves biliary excretion followed by reabsorption from intestine. Bacterial glucuronidases hydrolyze conjugates, releasing parent compound

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding excretion EXCEPT:

options.A: Breast milk serves as a route of elimination for lipophilic xenobiotics

explanation: Breast milk serves as a route of elimination for lipophilic xenobiotics. This is also a route of infant exposure

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding excretion EXCEPT:

options.B: Fecal excretion includes nonabsorbed ingesta, biliary excretion, and direct intestinal secretion

explanation: Fecal excretion includes nonabsorbed ingesta, biliary excretion, and direct intestinal secretion. MRP2 and BCRP actively secrete compounds into intestinal lumen

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Toxicokinetics is the quantitative study of ADME through measurement of concentrations in biological matrices vs time

explanation: Toxicokinetics is the quantitative study of ADME through measurement of concentrations in biological matrices vs time. Derived from pharmacokinetics studies with drugs

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cmax and AUC are the two most common dose metrics in toxicokinetic studies
options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Cmax and AUC are the two most common dose metrics in toxicokinetic studies. Cmax is peak concentration; AUC is area under concentration-time curve

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.D: The trapezoidal method calculates AUC by summing areas of trapezoids from the concentration-time curve

explanation: The trapezoidal method calculates AUC by summing areas of trapezoids from the concentration-time curve. AUC0-inf adds Clast/Kel for terminal area

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Mean residence time (MRT) = AUMC/AUC. AUMC is area under first moment curve (concentration x time)

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: At least 2 early and 3 terminal elimination phase time points needed for TK studies

explanation: At least 2 early and 3 terminal elimination phase time points needed for TK studies. Samples should show concentration changes by factor of 2 or order of magnitude

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.B: No more than 10% of blood volume should be drawn during AUC sampling interval

explanation: No more than 10% of blood volume should be drawn during AUC sampling interval. Prevents compromising physiological status

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: One-compartment model assumes body as single homogeneous compartment with instantaneous distribution
options.D: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: One-compartment model assumes body as single homogeneous compartment with instantaneous distribution. Appropriate for rapidly distributing compounds

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating toxicokinetics should consider which of the following?

options.B: PBTK models incorporate actual anatomical and physiological parameters (tissue volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients)

explanation: PBTK models incorporate actual anatomical and physiological parameters (tissue volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients). Allows mechanistic prediction of tissue concentrations

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating toxicokinetics should consider which of the following?

options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.D: Clearance is the volume of blood completely cleared of chemical per unit time

explanation: Clearance is the volume of blood completely cleared of chemical per unit time. Hepatic clearance depends on intrinsic clearance, blood flow, and protein binding

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating toxicokinetics should consider which of the following?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.B: Elimination half-life: t1/2 = 0.693/ke for first-order elimination

explanation: Elimination half-life: t1/2 = 0.693/ke for first-order elimination. Half-life doubles when clearance decreases by half

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating toxicokinetics should consider which of the following?

options.A: Bioavailability F = AUC_oral / (AUC_IV x dose_oral/dose_IV) x 100%
options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Bioavailability F = AUC_oral / (AUC_IV x dose_oral/dose_IV) x 100%. F < 100% indicates incomplete absorption or first-pass metabolism

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating toxicokinetics should consider which of the following?

options.A: Nonlinear kinetics occur when elimination processes become saturated at high doses
options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Nonlinear kinetics occur when elimination processes become saturated at high doses. AUC increases disproportionately; half-life may increase

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating air pollution should consider which of the following?

options.A: No health effects at ambient levels
options.D: PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 because smaller particles penetrate deeper into alveoli

explanation: PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 because smaller particles penetrate deeper into alveoli. PM10 is largely deposited in upper airways

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating air pollution should consider which of the following?

options.B: No health effects at ambient levels
options.D: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of NOx and VOCs

explanation: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of NOx and VOCs. Causes respiratory inflammation and decreased lung function
